mcqs.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the Fabaceae (legume) family?

options.A: Flowers with five fused petals and a superior ovary
options.B: Leaves that are alternate, simple, and lack stipules
options.C: Fruit that is a legume (pod) which splits open along two sutures
options.D: Fruit that is a fleshy berry

mcqs.answer: Fruit that is a legume (pod) which splits open along two sutures
mcqs.explanation: Fabaceae are identified by their fruit type – a legume (pod) that dehisces along two seams. Options A and B describe other families, and D is not typical of Fabaceae.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a typical characteristic of the Solanaceae family?

options.A: Flowers are actinomorphic with five fused petals and a superior ovary
options.B: Leaves are usually compound with tendrils

mcqs.answer: Flowers are actinomorphic with five fused petals and a superior ovary
mcqs.explanation: Solanaceae (nightshade family) have regular (actinomorphic) flowers with five fused petals and a superior ovary. The other options describe traits of unrelated families.

mcqs.question: Which floral feature distinguishes members of the Liliaceae family from those of the Fabaceae family?

options.B: Flowers with six tepals and a superior ovary

mcqs.answer: Flowers with six tepals and a superior ovary
mcqs.explanation: Liliaceae typically have flowers with six tepals (undifferentiated petals and sepals) and a superior ovary. Fabaceae have a legume fruit, not six tepals.

mcqs.question: Which combination of floral characters is diagnostic for the Solanaceae family?

options.A: Five sepals, five fused petals, and a superior ovary
options.B: Four sepals, four fused petals, and an inferior ovary
options.C: Five sepals, five free petals, and a superior ovary
options.D: Six sepals, six fused petals, and an inferior ovary

mcqs.answer: Five sepals, five fused petals, and a superior ovary
mcqs.explanation: Solanaceae flowers characteristically have five sepals, five petals that are fused (forming a tube), and a superior ovary. The other options do not match this pattern.

mcqs.question: Which of the following plants is NOT an economically important member of the Fabaceae family?
mcqs.explanation: Pea, soybean, and groundnut are all Fabaceae members with major agricultural value. Tomato belongs to the Solanaceae family, so it is not a Fabaceae member.

mcqs.question: A farmer observes a climbing plant with compound leaves, prominent stipules, and pods that split open along two seams when mature. To which family does this plant most likely belong?
mcqs.explanation: Compound leaves with stipules and dehiscent pods (legumes) are hallmark traits of Fabaceae. Solanaceae and Liliaceae lack these features, and Poaceae are grasses with spikelets, not pods.

mcqs.question: Statement: "All members of the Solanaceae family have compound leaves." Is this statement correct?
mcqs.explanation: Solanaceae exhibit a wide range of leaf types, most commonly simple leaves. Compound leaves are not a universal trait, making the statement false.

mcqs.question: If a flowering plant has six tepals, a superior ovary, and produces a capsule as its fruit, which family is it most likely to belong to?
mcqs.explanation: The combination of six tepals, a superior ovary, and a capsule fruit is characteristic of Liliaceae. Fabaceae have legumes, Solanaceae have berries or capsules but usually five petals, and Asteraceae have composite heads.
